newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia, Pakistan to tighten trade ties.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia, Pakistan to tighten trade ties.

text.p: Malaysia and Pakistan have agreed to improve trade and investment cooperation, Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi said on Thursday.
Badawi said the agreements involved the diversification of imports and exports, joint ventures and the relocation of labour intensive industries, the national Bernama news agency reported.

The announcement of closer ties came as Pakistan Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif arrived on Thursday for a three-day official visit to Malaysia, accompanied by a 50-member entourage of ministers and businessmen.
Malaysia and Pakistan on Thursday concluded a three-day trade meeting here.

Balance of trade between the two countries stood at $650 million for the 1995-96 period. Pakistan imports from Malaysia totalled $708 million, while exports amounted to $56 million for the same period.
Pakistan is seeking to increase its exports of commodities such as rice and fruits to Malaysia as the balance of trade was now in Malaysia's favour, Gohar told reporters after the meeting.

He said Pakistan was also looking into Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's suggestion that the two countries have joint production and collaboration in the processing and marketing of palm oil.
Also, apart from the possibility of supplying defence equipment to Malaysia, Gohar said Malaysian defence personnel could be trained in Pakistan.
He suggested that Malaysian investors establish joint-ventures or set up businesses in Pakistan including buying over industries which were being de-nationalised or privatised.
